### Technical detail
**Source:** IMPECT Customer API: `/iterations`, `/iterations/{id}/matches`, `/iterations/{id}/squads`
and `/matches/{id}/squad-kpis` (SHOT_XG, POSTSHOT_XG, shots…). UAE Pro League only.

**Fixtures:** if IMPECT only publishes part of the schedule, the missing fixtures are completed assuming
a double round-robin league, without inventing dates. Team strengths are kept constant,
so the order of the remaining matches does not change the final distribution.

**Team strength (model v4):** for every match played the evidence is
`0.8 × xG + 0.2 × goals` (goals only if there is no xG). PSxG is not used: it predicts worse in the backtest.
Mix, prior (12 matches) and weight of past seasons (0.3 / 0.09) chosen by backtest. The current season weighs 1 and previous
complete seasons 0.3 / 0.09 / 0.027. Separate averages for home and away goals.
Attack = (weighted evidence for + prior × starting level) / (goals expected by venue + prior),
and the same for defence. Prior = 12 equivalent matches. The starting level comes from the **IMPECT ISR** on the date of the last match played:
attack = exp(3 × (ISR − mean)), defence = exp(−3 × (ISR − mean)). The factor 3 was chosen in the backtest
(2 and 4 give almost the same; 6 or 8 are worse). Without ISR, the league average or the historical level of promoted teams is used.

**Simulation:** in every simulated season each team's attack and defence are perturbed with
log-normal noise of deviation ≈ 1/√(evidence), reflecting that their true level is uncertain.
Goals in each remaining match ~ Poisson(home mean × home attack × away defence), capped at 0.15–5.
Fixed seed: results are reproducible.

**Title and positions:** the title % splits ties on points equally; the official tie-break is not applied yet.
Final positions are ordered by points, goal difference and goals scored.

**«Title chances if we finish on X points»:** probability that no rival goes above X
(ties split), using all simulations. It is a relationship within the model, not a guarantee.

**ISR and rescalings:** IMPECT sometimes recalibrates the ISR scale of the whole league at once
(e.g. September 2026). Since the model uses each team's distance to the league average on the same
date, those rescalings do not affect it; absolute values from different dates are not comparable.

**Validation:** the backtest reruns the model on finished seasons using only the first
matchdays and compares with what happened. With only two complete seasons, it is an indicative check.

**Limitations:** it does not account for signings, injuries, coaching changes or sanctions; it does not adjust for
the difficulty of opponents already played or for recent form within the season.

1. Each player's score (PV LEAGUE, 0–100)
PV LEAGUE = 0.40·pct(ELO) + 0.10·pct(ELO trend) + 0.40·pct(value) + 0.10·pct(value trend)
Each «pct» is the player's percentile within his group: same season, same age cohort and same position, among all players in the league. Example: a centre-back born in 1999–02 is only compared with the 1999–02 centre-backs in the league that season. An 80 means he is above 80% of his peers.
2. The team score (average PV LEAGUE)
Average PV LEAGUE (team, season) = simple mean of the PV LEAGUE of its players with minutes that season.
3. How to read it
· 50 = average squad: its players are, on average, on par with those of their age and position in the league.
· 70 = its players are, on average, above 70% of their peers. A top squad.
· Since they are percentiles within the league, it measures the level relative to each season's league, not an absolute level.
4. Why PV LEAGUE and not PV TEAM or PV AVG
· PV TEAM compares each player only with his club team-mates: every team has players above and below, so its mean always comes out around 50 and is no use to compare teams.
· PV AVG is half PV LEAGUE and half PV TEAM: it carries that 50 and halves the differences between teams.

Verdict: market value does predict: almost as well as the ISR over the season (accuracy 8.2% vs 8.1%), and far better than using nothing (4.0%). But with 5 matchdays the ISR is better (9.0% vs 8.0%, and it gave 40% to the actual champion vs 25%): money separates big from small teams well, but is worse at telling which of the big ones wins. Adding both barely improves (8.3%) and at matchday 5 it gets slightly worse, so the main model stays with the ISR and the market remains an alternative view.
Note: in past seasons minutes are from the whole season (including winter signings), which slightly favours the market in the test. Even so it does not beat the ISR at matchday 5.
Intensidad calibrada con 24/25 y 25/26:: Strength calibrated with 24/25 and 25/26: each time a squad is worth double, it generates ≈27% more goals and concedes ≈22% less (before correcting for matches played). In the matchday-5 test it predicts somewhat worse than the ISR (see below, in the Transfermarkt tab).
